newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa ups some air cargo rates by 10pct.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa ups some air cargo rates by 10pct.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo said it will raise ex-Germany air cargo rates by up to 10 percent on selected routes from October 1.
The move is an attempt to push up ex-Germany market rates which have fallen dramatically in recent months, the Deutsche Lufthansa AG cargo arm said in a statement.
Rates to Bangkok, Hong Kong and Singapore will go up by just under 10 percent, it said.
Prices to Copenhagen, Oslo and London will be increased by between five and 10 percent, the statement said.
Lufthansa Cargo said it will also adjust rates to other destinations according to weight categories.
Some rates to Brazil and Canada will thus increase by about five percent, it said.
Lufthansa Cargo said it will in future invoice separately for certain product groups such as textiles (hanging garments), bulk shipments, automobiles and motorcycles.
This is because these types of shipments involve additional services and expenditure, including on handling, the airline explained.

The statement added: "By implementing this pricing strategy, Lufthansa Cargo is reacting to the developments in recent months in which rates, especially in the ad hoc sector, have fallen to a significantly lower level.
"In view of the expected increase in freight volume and the decline in capacities in future, the rate increase is a logical step towards countering the ruinous price competition."
